title: The Doves Who Flew Away with the Net
text:
A flock of doves was led by a king named Chitragriva. One day, flying over a forest, they saw grains of rice scattered on the ground, a fine meal for hungry birds. They swooped down to eat, and a hunter's net, hidden under the grain, fell over them all.

The doves panicked, each beating its wings and pulling in a different direction, which only tangled them further. Chitragriva called out to stop. Struggling alone, he said, no one would escape. But if they all rose together at the same moment, they could carry the net with them. On his signal the whole flock lifted off at once, and the net rose into the air with them while the hunter on the ground ran after them until he lost sight of the flock.

Chitragriva led them to his friend Hiranyaka, a mouse who lived nearby. The mouse wanted to free the king first, but Chitragriva refused and asked him to free his followers before him, in case the mouse grew tired. Hiranyaka gnawed through the cords one by one until every dove was free, and the flock flew home.
lesson: A trap that holds individuals can often be overcome by a group acting at the same moment. A good leader makes sure his people are safe before himself.
people: Chitragriva the dove king, the doves, Hiranyaka the mouse
source: Panchatantra, Book II (The Winning of Friends)
